title: Tensoring a K-flat quasi-isomorphism with an arbitrary complex
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, regarded as a sheaf of rings on the one-point site, let $N^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $R$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and let $\alpha:E^\bullet\to E'^\bullet$ be a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] between K-flat complexes of $R$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Then the induced map of total complexes $\operatorname{Tot}(\alpha\otimes 1_N):\operatorname{Tot}(E^\bullet\otimes_R N^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Tot}(E'^\bullet\otimes_R N^\bullet)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: Throughout, $R$ is regarded as a sheaf of rings on the one-point site, whose sheaves of modules are the $R$-modules; so [def-pc-kflat-complex], [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and the cited lemmas about complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules apply to complexes of $R$-modules. (Symmetry.) For complexes $F^\bullet,G^\bullet$ of $R$-modules let $\sigma_{F,G}:\operatorname{Tot}(F^\bullet\otimes_R G^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Tot}(G^\bullet\otimes_R F^\bullet)$ be $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ on $F^p\otimes_R G^q$. It is a chain map: for $x\in F^p$, $y\in G^q$, $d(x\otimes y)=d_Fx\otimes y+(-1)^p x\otimes d_Gy$ is sent to $(-1)^{(p+1)q}y\otimes d_Fx+(-1)^{p+p(q+1)}d_Gy\otimes x$, while $d((-1)^{pq}y\otimes x)=(-1)^{pq}d_Gy\otimes x+(-1)^{pq+q}y\otimes d_Fx$, and the two agree since $(-1)^{p+p(q+1)}=(-1)^{pq}$. It is an isomorphism with inverse $\sigma_{G,F}$, and it is natural in both variables: $\sigma_{F',G'}\circ\operatorname{Tot}(f\otimes g)=\operatorname{Tot}(g\otimes f)\circ\sigma_{F,G}$ for chain maps $f:F\to F'$, $g:G\to G'$ (the sign depends only on the degrees, which $f,g$ preserve). Consequently, for a chain map $f$ and a complex $G$, $\operatorname{Tot}(f\otimes 1_G)$ is a quasi-isomorphism if and only if $\operatorname{Tot}(1_G\otimes f)$ is (they are conjugate by the isomorphisms $\sigma$), and $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes G)$ is acyclic if and only if $\operatorname{Tot}(G\otimes F)$ is. (Mathlib's form of this symmetry is HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctorFlipIso with its naturality mapBifunctorFlipIso_hom_naturality, Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/BifunctorFlip.lean.)

proof.text: (Tag 06Y0, lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism, in both variables.) Let $K^\bullet$ be a K-flat complex of $R$-modules and $s:L^\bullet\to L'^\bullet$ a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of $R$-modules. Then $\operatorname{Tot}(1_K\otimes s)$ and $\operatorname{Tot}(s\otimes 1_K)$ are quasi-isomorphisms. Indeed, the mapping cone $C(s)$ is acyclic because $s$ is a quasi-isomorphism [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]; hence $\operatorname{Tot}(C(s)\otimes_R K)$ is acyclic by the definition of K-flatness of $K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex], and so is $\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_R C(s))$ by step 1. By [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso] (with $\mathcal A^\bullet=K^\bullet$ and the morphism $s:L\to L'$), $\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_R C(s))$ is isomorphic as a complex to the mapping cone of $\operatorname{Tot}(1_K\otimes s):\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_R L)\to\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_R L')$, which is therefore acyclic, so $\operatorname{Tot}(1_K\otimes s)$ is a quasi-isomorphism [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]. By step 1, $\operatorname{Tot}(s\otimes 1_K)$ is a quasi-isomorphism as well.

proof.text: The square $$\begin{array}{ccc}\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes_R K)&\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Tot}(\alpha\otimes 1_K)}&\operatorname{Tot}(E'\otimes_R K)\\ \downarrow{\scriptstyle\operatorname{Tot}(1_E\otimes s)}&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle\operatorname{Tot}(1_{E'}\otimes s)}\\ \operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes_R N)&\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Tot}(\alpha\otimes 1_N)}&\operatorname{Tot}(E'\otimes_R N)\end{array}$$ commutes, both composites being $\operatorname{Tot}(\alpha\otimes s)$, since on each summand $E^p\otimes K^q$ both are $\alpha^p\otimes s^q$ (functoriality of the total tensor complex in both variables [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]).

In the square of step 4 the vertical arrows are quasi-isomorphisms by step 2 applied to the K-flat complex $E$ (resp. $E'$) and the quasi-isomorphism $s$ (the form $\operatorname{Tot}(1_E\otimes s)$), and the top arrow is a quasi-isomorphism by step 2 applied to the K-flat complex $K$ and the quasi-isomorphism $\alpha$ (the form $\operatorname{Tot}(\alpha\otimes 1_K)$). Taking cohomology in degree $i$, $H^i(\operatorname{Tot}(\alpha\otimes 1_N))\circ H^i(\operatorname{Tot}(1_E\otimes s))=H^i(\operatorname{Tot}(1_{E'}\otimes s))\circ H^i(\operatorname{Tot}(\alpha\otimes 1_K))$ with the three maps other than the first isomorphisms, so $H^i(\operatorname{Tot}(\alpha\otimes 1_N))$ is an isomorphism for every $i$, i.e. $\operatorname{Tot}(\alpha\otimes 1_N)$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. (Stacks states the lemma with $\alpha$ in the second factor, $\operatorname{Tot}(1_L\otimes\alpha)$; the item's form with $\alpha$ in the first factor is the same argument, and either form follows from the other by step 1.)
